newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks get lift from properties in morning.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks get lift from properties in morning.

text.p: Gains in the property sector boosted Hong Kong share prices in Thursday morning trade, with investors taking their cue from higher prices on Wall Street.
The Hang Seng index was up 63.75 points at 12,829.77. Turnover was HK$2.35 billion after the first hour of trade.
"We don't have much trend of our own so we are just following overseas markets," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Dow industrials rose 38.44 points to 6,346.77 on Wednesday.
Property stocks led the rise with Sun Hung Kai Properties up HK$1.00 at HK$91.75. Henderson Land rose HK$0.25 to HK$72.25.

Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities, said investors may take a move by Sun Hung Kai Properties to curb speculation in the property market as a sign that the government "will not come up with harsh measures" of its own.

Sun Hung Kai Properties said it would implement a new registration system for its latest sale of residential flats at East Point City in Tseung Kwan O restricting the number of potential home buyers registering under limited companies to a maximum of 20 for every 100 registered buyers.
"That will give the impression that the government is really trying to force them (property developers) to regulate themselves," said Tsang.

Brokers said share prices would probably see limited upside during the session, with investors winding down ahead of the Christmas holiday period and following the Hong Kong market's strong performance this year. "Most participants are not doing much in this market," said Mak.
Shares in HSBC Holdings rose HK$1.00 to HK$156.00 and Hang Seng Bank was up HK$0.50 at HK$90.00.
